misconceptions.description: Thinking the value of two AI tools is doubling the number of automatic edits rather than surfacing disagreement
misconceptions.trigger: learner applies every edit from both tools without comparing them
misconceptions.feedback: The point of two tools is the comparison. Look at where they agree and disagree, and treat disagreement as a decision you must make.

misconceptions.description: Resolving a conflict between two tools by trusting whichever sounds more positive or more confident
misconceptions.trigger: learner picks the friendlier or more authoritative critique instead of checking it against the goal
misconceptions.feedback: Neither tool knows your target audience. Resolve conflicts against the job posting or rubric, not against tone.

misconceptions.description: Assuming that when both tools agree, you must apply the fix even if it means inventing information
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds a fabricated metric because both tools requested one
misconceptions.feedback: Agreement signals a real gap, but the fix must stay truthful. Log the valid critique and find a real number before adding one.

misconceptions.description: Writing a critique log that does not name each tool's suggestion, the decision, or the concrete change
misconceptions.trigger: learner records "used AI to fix it" with no comparison or reason
misconceptions.feedback: Log each tool's suggestion, your decision, the exact change, and what you rejected, so a reader can follow your judgment.
